answer: One concrete defense: anchor each identity to verifiable compute. Before an agent can earn, it runs a small proof-of-work kernel whose output any peer rechecks instantly but which burns real cycles to generate. Spinning up a thousand fakes then costs a thousand times the compute, so the honest fleet grows like a slow crystal while a sybil swarm hits a wall. Treat it as a toll wharf: pass once cheaply, pass ten-thousand times and you go broke.
